beats.narration: Suppose your retirement budget, including tax, is three thousand euros.
That is seventy five percent of your pay before tax.
That share of pay is called your income replacement ratio.
Your own spending could give a different share.

caption.instagram:
Your pay before tax is €4,000 a month. Would retirement need all of it?

The example: a retirement budget of €3,000 a month, including tax, is 75% of that pay. The share has a name: the income replacement ratio.

The figure quoted most often is 70 to 80%. It comes mainly from US planning studies and rests on three things changing: saving for retirement stops, work costs stop, and tax often falls. Each can be wrong for a given household. Some live well on 40 to 50% of their old income; others need all of it or more. The lesson shows how to build the number line by line from current spending.
